prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1330; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the scene in Pearland, Texas, I found two vehicles that had come together in a low-speed head-on collision. Driver 1 was standing beside a vehicle with front-end damage that matched the impact described by both drivers. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and said the belt tightened sharply during the collision. The injury appears consistent with the kind and force of this crash. Driver 2 reported no earlier damage to the vehicle, and I found no information suggesting any prior damage to either car. Passenger was in Driver 2's vehicle and reported no injuries. Driver 1 could not say clearly where in the vehicle they were seated at the moment of impact, and that detail remains unclear. Scene photographs confirm the positions of both vehicles and some of the damage. No independent witnesses were located. Driver 1 is named on the insurance policy covering the vehicle involved.
